1	# Architecture
2	
3	How the AI Robot Redesign Engine is put together. For the plan, demo script, milestones and team split, see [HANDOFF-v2.md](HANDOFF-v2.md). For policy facts, prize rules and TinyFish limits, see [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md) (v1). For Entire commands, see [ENTIRE.md](ENTIRE.md).
4	
5	## 1. Overview
6	
7	An engineer has a robot whose drive motor must be replaced to meet US sourcing rules. The system:
8	
9	1. shows **why** the part has to go: a compliance card (FCC coverage, domestic-content % against the 65% and 75% lines, the US final-assembly requirement) and a **separate** supply-risk flag (for example NdFeB magnets)
10	2. sends a **TinyFish agent swarm** to find real NEMA-frame replacement motors on live manufacturer and distributor websites, extract their specs, and verify origin and price against the source page
11	3. runs **deterministic engineering checks** (torque, speed, voltage, fit) and labels each candidate Rejected / Review / Pass\*
12	4. **regenerates the robot's CAD** in CadQuery: a new motor mounting bracket sized to the chosen motor, exported as GLB for the browser and STEP for engineers
13	5. runs a small **tournament** of 2–3 designs (lowest cost, best performance, US-first) and shows them side by side in 3D
14	6. drafts an RFQ for the chosen supplier and holds it for approval
15	
16	Hackathon scope: one small wheeled robot that we model ourselves, and one subsystem (drive motor + bracket). This is a parametric template, not general editing of uploaded CAD files.
17	
18	## 2. Diagram
19	
20	```mermaid
21	flowchart LR
22	  U[Engineer] -->|robot params, BOM, requirements| API
23	
24	  subgraph Vultr[Vultr compute]
25	    API[Orchestrator API] --> CMP[Compliance card]
26	    API --> PLAN[Search planner]
27	    PLAN --> SW[Agent swarm]
28	    SW --> VF[Verifier]
29	    VF --> CHK[Engineering checks]
30	    CHK --> TRN[Tournament]
31	    TRN --> CAD[CAD workers: CadQuery]
32	  end
33	
34	  PLAN -->|requirements| GEM[Gemini]
35	  SW <-->|TinySearch, TinyFetch, TinyAgent| WEB[(Manufacturer and distributor sites)]
36	  SW -->|datasheet PDFs| GEM
37	  VF -->|re-fetch html, string-match| WEB
38	  MON[TinyMonitor: chosen motor page] -->|price, stock changes| TS
39	
40	  CAD -->|GLB, STEP| OBJ[(Vultr Object Storage)]
41	  VF -->|html evidence| OBJ
42	
43	  SW & CHK -->|runs, prices, check results| TS[(Tiger Data)]
44	
45	  TRN --> RFQ[RFQ draft: Gemini]
46	  RFQ -->|TinyBrowser fills form, stops before submit| A0[Auth0: manager approves]
47	
48	  OBJ --> FE[Frontend: 3D viewer, live tiles, comparison]
49	  TS --> FE
50	  CMP --> FE
51	```
52	
53	## 3. Components
54	
55	| # | Component | What it does | Deterministic or LLM | Owner |
56	|---|---|---|---|---|
57	| 1 | Robot model | Parametric CadQuery robot (base plate, wheels, motor mounts, electronics box) plus its BOM and requirements (mass, wheel radius, gear ratio, top speed, bus voltage, chassis envelope). | Deterministic | CAD |
58	| 2 | Compliance card | Checks FCC coverage, computes domestic % by component cost (unknown origin = foreign), shows the US final-assembly requirement, and flags supply risks on a separate track. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
59	| 3 | Search planner | Turns the motor requirements into search queries and target sites. Seeded with 2–3 pre-identified real motors. | Gemini | Agents |
60	| 4 | Agent swarm | TinySearch + TinyFetch for broad discovery; TinyAgent for product pages and datasheets, returning the motor `output_schema`; live `streaming_url` tiles. | TinyFish | Agents |
61	| 5 | Datasheet reader | Reads datasheet PDFs and spec-table images when the product page lacks specs, and returns strict JSON. | Gemini (multimodal) | Agents |
62	| 6 | Verifier | Fetches the source page again and string-matches origin, price and NEMA frame against the html. Saves the html as evidence. | Deterministic | Agents |
63	| 7 | Engineering checks | Torque, speed, voltage and fit checks (§5) give Rejected / Review / Pass\*, plus a fit badge (`drop_in` / `close` / `needs_review`) and a spec comparison table. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
64	| 8 | Tournament | Picks the best passing candidate for each objective: lowest cost, best performance, US-first. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
65	| 9 | CAD workers | Regenerate the bracket and assembly for each design using the NEMA lookup table, then export GLB and STEP. One job per design, run in parallel. | Deterministic (CadQuery) | CAD |
66	| 10 | Writer | Fit explanations, the design comparison write-up and the RFQ draft. Numbers are passed in, never computed. | Gemini | Agents |
67	| 11 | RFQ flow | TinyBrowser + Playwright fills one supplier's quote form and stops before submitting. Auth0 approval is required to send. | TinyFish + Auth0 | Agents |
68	| 12 | Frontend | Compliance card, live agent tiles, check results table, 3D viewer with before/after slider, design tabs, Tiger Data panels. | n/a | Frontend + infra |
69	
70	## 4. Data flow and schemas
71	
72	**Robot requirements (input)**
73	
74	| Field | Type | Notes |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| `mass_kg` | number | robot mass including payload |
77	| `wheel_radius_m` | number | |
78	| `n_drive_motors` | int | |
79	| `gear_ratio` | number | `G` |
80	| `efficiency` | number | drivetrain `η` |
81	| `crr` | number | rolling resistance |
82	| `max_slope_deg` | number | `θ` |
83	| `accel_mps2` | number | target acceleration `a` |
84	| `v_max_mps` | number | top speed |
85	| `bus_voltage_v` | number | |
86	| `envelope_mm` | number | space available for motor + bracket |
87	| `safety_factor` | number | about 1.5 |
88	
89	**BOM row (input)**
90	
91	| Field | Type | Notes |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| `part` | string | |
94	| `category` | string | motor, gearbox, encoder, battery, compute, sensor, frame and so on |
95	| `qty` | int | |
96	| `unit_cost_usd` | decimal | |
97	| `origin` | ISO country code or `unknown` | `unknown` counts as foreign; Canadian parts count as foreign |
98	| `supply_risk` | string? | for example `ndfeb_magnets`. Shown separately; does not change domestic % |
99	
100	**Agent `output_schema` (one per candidate motor)**
101	
102	A run that reports `COMPLETED` has not necessarily met its goal, so every result carries its own status. Data fields are optional so the agent doesn't fill unreachable ones with placeholders.
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "status": "success | blocked | not_found | auth_required | incomplete",
107	  "reason": "string",
108	  "manufacturer": "string?",
109	  "part_number": "string?",
110	  "nema_frame": "string? (17 | 23 | 34)",
111	  "body_length_mm": "number?",
112	  "rated_torque_nm": "number?",
113	  "rated_speed_rpm": "number?",
114	  "voltage_v": "number?",
115	  "shaft_diameter_mm": "number?",
116	  "price_usd": "number?",
117	  "lead_time_days": "number?",
118	  "country_of_origin": "string?",
119	  "origin_quote": "string? (exact text from the page)",
120	  "product_url": "string?",
121	  "datasheet_url": "string?"
122	}
123	```
124	
125	**Verifier statuses:** `verified`, `price_mismatch`, `origin_not_found`, `frame_mismatch`, `blocked`, `rejected`. Only `verified` candidates reach the engineering checks.
126	
127	**Check result (per candidate):** `verdict` (`rejected | review | pass`), `fit` (`drop_in | close | needs_review`), and one row per check with `value`, `threshold`, `pass` and source links.
128	
129	**Design variant (per tournament entry):** `design_id`, `objective` (`cost | performance | us_first`), `motor` (part number), `cost_usd`, `domestic_pct`, `glb_url`, `step_url`.
130	
131	**Tiger Data**
132	
133	- `agent_runs` (hypertable): `time`, `run_id`, `site`, `product`, `status`, `duration_s`, `steps`.
134	- `site_success_hourly` (continuous aggregate over `agent_runs`): powers the "success rate by site" panel, which is also evidence that the agents hold up on live websites.
135	- `price_observations` (hypertable): `time`, `part_number`, `supplier`, `price_usd`, `lead_time_days`, `origin`, `run_id`. Filled by repeated runs and TinyMonitor events.
136	- `check_results` (hypertable): `time`, `design_id`, `candidate`, `check`, `value`, `threshold`, `pass`. The audit trail behind each verdict.
137	- `design_variants` (regular table in the same database): the design variant fields above.
138	
139	## 5. Engineering checks and CAD
140	
141	**Checks** (all code; symbols from the requirements table):
142	
143	| Check | Pass if |
144	|---|---|
145	| Torque | `r·m·(g·(Crr·cosθ + sinθ) + a) / (n·G·η) · SF ≤ rated_torque_nm` |
146	| Speed | `(rated_speed_rpm / G) · 2πr / 60 ≥ v_max` |
147	| Voltage | `voltage_v` matches `bus_voltage_v` (or is within the driver's supported range) |
148	| Fit | `body_length_mm + bracket thickness + clearance ≤ envelope_mm`, and `nema_frame` is in the lookup table |
149	
150	**NEMA lookup table.** Typical values. Check each one against a real vendor drawing before building.
151	
152	| Frame | Bolt-hole spacing (square) | Pilot diameter | Common shaft diameter |
153	|---|---|---|---|
154	| NEMA 17 | 31.0 mm | 22.0 mm | 5 mm |
155	| NEMA 23 | 47.14 mm | 38.1 mm | 6.35 mm or 8 mm |
156	| NEMA 34 | 69.6 mm | 73.0 mm | 9.5 / 12.7 / 14 mm |
157	
158	**CAD functions** (CadQuery):
159	
160	- `robot(params)`: the full assembly
161	- `motor(frame, body_len)`: a simple motor body from the NEMA table
162	- `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`: bolt spacing and pilot hole from the NEMA table; width from the frame; depth and position from `body_len`
163	
164	Export: `cq.Assembly` to **GLB** for the viewer and **STEP** for the engineering export. The viewer (`<model-viewer>` or three.js) highlights the changed bracket and has a before/after slider.
165	
166	## 6. Hard rules
167	
168	1. The LLM never does arithmetic. All costs, percentages, checks and optimization are plain code.
169	2. Pass/fail comes from code checks and documented specs, never from an LLM's judgment.
170	3. Unknown origin counts as foreign. Allied content does not count, so Canadian parts are foreign.
171	4. Compliance and supply risk are separate. A US-made motor with foreign magnets still counts as domestic under the component test (confirm with counsel before stating it on stage).
172	5. A domestic end product must also be manufactured in the US. The compliance card says so whenever the robot is built elsewhere.
173	6. Every number in the UI links to its source. Nothing unverified reaches the checks.
174	7. Bolt patterns come from the NEMA lookup table, not from an LLM reading drawings.
175	8. No RFQ is submitted without Auth0 approval. One honest identity on real vendor sites; no fake personas.
176	9. The UI says "not legal advice" and "Pass\* = passes the checks we implemented, not engineering certification". The COTS question is shown as "flag for counsel".
177	10. No API keys or TinyFish credentials in prompts, because Entire session transcripts are pushed with the code.
178	
179	## 7. Where each sponsor fits
180	
181	| Sponsor | Where it runs | Where it is deliberately not used |
182	|---|---|---|
183	| TinyFish | TinySearch + TinyFetch for discovery; TinyAgent for product pages and datasheets with live tiles; TinyFetch html for verification; TinyBrowser for the RFQ form; TinyMonitor on the chosen motor's page | Broad discovery doesn't use Agent runs (cost and concurrency) |
184	| Gemini | Search planning; multimodal datasheet reading with strict JSON; long-context comparison of 3–5 datasheets; fit explanations, comparison write-up, RFQ draft | Arithmetic, pass/fail verdicts, origin verification, bolt patterns |
185	| Vultr | Orchestrator API (FastAPI) and workers in Docker (CadQuery/OCCT image); tournament designs as parallel CAD jobs; Object Storage for GLB/STEP files, datasheets and html evidence | n/a |
186	| Tiger Data | Hypertables for agent runs, prices and check results; continuous aggregate for site success rate; relational `design_variants` in the same database | n/a |
187	| Auth0 | Auth0 for AI Agents: manager approval before the RFQ is submitted; roles (engineer drafts, manager approves) | n/a |
188	| Entire | Trails per feature with review agents, overnight session handoffs, Brain for key decisions, graph search with measured token savings | n/a |
189	| GoDaddy | Live domain hosting the demo | n/a |
190	
191	## 8. Limits and fallbacks
192	
193	| Limit | How we handle it |
194	|---|---|
195	| About 2 concurrent TinyFish Agent runs and 5 Browser sessions on standard accounts | Queue runs with `/run-batch`. Ask the booth for a hackathon increase. Otherwise fill the tile wall with Browser sessions and cached replays, and say which tiles are live. |
196	| No CAPTCHA solving | Mark the site `blocked` and move on. Prefer sites with no bot wall (test in hour one). |
197	| `max_steps` needs beta access | Use `max_duration_seconds` (GA) as the run limit. |
198	| No screenshots | Store the captured `html` as evidence and use it for the verifier string-match. |
199	| File upload in TinyAgent is unclear | Use TinyBrowser + Playwright `setInputFiles`. |
200	| Datasheet dimensions misread | Only frame size, body length and ratings come from the web; bolt patterns come from the NEMA table. Mismatches go to Review. |
201	| The swarm comes up empty on demo day | 2–3 real motors are pre-identified and seeded into the planner. |
202	| CadQuery install pain | Run it in a Docker image on Vultr, so nobody installs OCCT locally. |
203	| Live websites fail during the demo | Pre-run and cache demo inputs; record a backup video. |
204	
205	## 9. Repo layout
206	
207	> **Stub:** fill in once the stack is chosen. One folder per owner from the team split in HANDOFF-v2.md:
208	>
209	> 1. CAD: parametric robot, bracket generator, GLB/STEP export, viewer
210	> 2. Agents: TinyFish swarm, datasheet reader, verifier, RFQ flow
211	> 3. Engineering + data: checks, tournament, NEMA table, compliance card, demo robot requirements, Tiger Data schema
212	> 4. Frontend + infra: UI, live tiles, comparison view, Vultr deployment
213

1	# Entire CLI reference
2	
3	Commands for using the Entire CLI (`entire`) in this repo. The GitHub repo is `Kingsolima/HackWestern-2026`.
4	
5	Values in `<angle brackets>` only exist at run time. Get them from the output of an earlier command:
6	
7	- `<id>`: a finding or checkpoint ID, from `entire trail finding` or `entire checkpoint list`
8	- `<branch>`: a teammate's branch name, from `git branch -a`
9	- `<trail-number>`: a Trail number, from `entire trail show` or entire.com
10	- `<commit>`: the short hash of the commit with the fix, from `git log --oneline`
11	
12	## Setup (once per machine)
13	
14	This is WSL with no OS keyring. `~/.config/entire/config.json` must contain `{"token_store": "file"}`, or the login won't be saved.
15	
16	```bash
17	entire login                       # opens a browser; a human has to finish it
18	entire repo mirror add             # needs the Entire GitHub App on the repo
19	```
20	
21	To clone a fresh copy:
22	
23	```bash
24	cd ~
25	entire repo clone /gh/Kingsolima/HackWestern-2026 --nearest
26	cd HackWestern-2026
27	```
28	
29	To enable Entire in an existing clone:
30	
31	```bash
32	entire enable                      # choose Claude Code
33	entire status                      # check that sessions are being captured
34	```
35	
36	## One Trail per feature
37	
38	Use a separate branch and Trail for each feature: the swarm, the verifier, the optimizer and the frontend. This example is for the swarm:
39	
40	```bash
41	git switch -c swap-finder-swarm
42	entire trail create --title "TinyFish swap-finder swarm" --type feature
43	entire trail watch                              # live reviews and findings
44	entire trail finding                            # list what review agents flagged
45	entire trail finding apply <id>                 # accept a suggested fix
46	entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in <commit>"
47	entire trail ready
48	entire trail merge
49	```
50	
51	Add Entire's preset review agents (risk, security, drift and others). The presets run on free credit:
52	
53	```bash
54	entire project agent add
55	```
56	
57	## Handing work between teammates
58	
59	```bash
60	entire session resume <branch>     # pick up a teammate's agent session with its full context
61	entire trail resume <trail-number> # continue a Trail with its sessions
62	```
63	
64	## Search past work before starting over
65	
66	```bash
67	entire search "why does the verifier reject unknown origin" --json --compact
68	entire checkpoint explain <id>
69	```
70	
71	## Proof for the Devpost page (before submitting)
72	
73	```bash
74	entire checkpoint list             # number of checkpoints
75	entire activity                    # activity overview and recent sessions
76	entire dispatch                    # written summary of recent agent work
77	entire trail show                  # screenshot a Trail page with its findings
78	```
79	
80	Take screenshots of the Trail pages on entire.com too.
81	
82	## Check what you're uploading
83	
84	Session transcripts are pushed with the code, so a public repo makes them public.
85	
86	```bash
87	entire checkpoint list --outgoing
88	```
89	
90	To keep transcripts in a separate private repo (create `Kingsolima/HackWestern-2026-sessions` on GitHub as a private repo first):
91	
92	```bash
93	entire configure --local --checkpoint-remote github:Kingsolima/HackWestern-2026-sessions
94	```
95	
96	If judges need to see sessions, keep the repo public. Make sure no API keys or TinyFish credentials ever appear in prompts.
97	
98	## Extras
99	
100	```bash
101	entire trail comment add -m "..."          # add to a Trail's discussion
102	entire trail attachment add shot.png       # attach a screenshot to a Trail
103	entire trail rerun-review                  # run the review agents again
104	entire plugin search                       # find plugins
105	entire plugin install <name>               # install a plugin
106	entire doctor                              # fix stuck sessions
107	entire api /api/v1/me                      # call the API directly
108	```
109

1	# Hack Western 13 handoff v2: AI Robot Redesign Engine
2	
3	Updated Sat Nov 21, 2026. Devpost deadline: **Sun Nov 22, 9am EST**.
4	
5	**What changed from v1:** we no longer just recommend US-made replacement parts. We **find a replacement, check that it works, and regenerate the robot's CAD to fit it.** The sourcing and compliance work from v1 becomes step 1 ("why this part has to go").
6	
7	**Still valid in [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md) (v1):** policy facts and sources (§2), prize rules and how to compete for each track (§3, §3a), TinyFish limits (§4), rejected ideas (§8). [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes the v1 design. Where it disagrees with this file, this file wins.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. The pitch
12	
13	> "This robot's drive motor has to be replaced to meet US sourcing rules. Finding another motor is easy. The hard part is knowing it actually works and changing the robot to fit it. Our AI engineer does both, live."
14	
15	**Hackathon scope:** a small wheeled robot. **One subsystem, the drive motor and its mounting bracket**, is redesigned end to end. Then we generate 2–3 competing designs (lowest cost, best performance, US-first).
16	
17	**Full product vision (pitch only, don't build):** upload any CAD assembly and BOM, redesign every affected subsystem, run simulation, and export for engineering review.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Simplifications (locked, don't reopen)
22	
23	1. **NEMA-standard motors only (NEMA 17 / 23 / 34).** The frame size fixes the bolt pattern, pilot diameter and shaft diameter. The agent only has to find **frame size, body length, torque, speed and voltage**, which are usually plain text on the page. Bolt patterns come from our lookup table (§6), not from Gemini reading drawings.
24	2. **We build the whole robot ourselves in CadQuery:** base plate, wheels, motor mounts, electronics box. Don't import GrabCAD models (painful to convert, license restrictions, not parametric). Clean and labelled is better than realistic.
25	3. **Parametric template, not general CAD editing.** The bracket is a function `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`. Be upfront about this in the pitch.
26	4. **One subsystem.** We show the whole robot, but only the motor mount changes.
27	5. **Four checks, all in code:** torque, speed, voltage and fit (§6). "Pass" means "passes the checks we implemented", and the UI says so.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 3. Fixes from review (build these into the design)
32	
33	1. **Magnets are a supply risk, not a compliance hit.** My understanding of the Buy American Act component test (confirm with counsel before saying it on stage): a component is domestic if *it* is made in the US, whatever its sub-parts (except iron and steel). A US-made motor with Chinese NdFeB magnets still counts as domestic. **Show two separate tracks:** "Compliance: 67% ✅" and "Supply risk: magnets ⚠️". Never mix them.
34	2. **US final assembly is required too.** A robot is a "domestic end product" only if it is **manufactured in the US** *and* more than 65% of its component cost is domestic. If the demo robot is Canadian-built, the verdict must say "also needs US final assembly." Canadian parts count as foreign.
35	3. **Every swap gets a fit badge:** `drop_in` / `close` / `needs_review`, with a spec comparison table (for example "torque 0.28 vs 0.30 Nm (−7%)"). The code checks decide pass or fail. Gemini only writes the explanation.
36	4. **Concurrency fallback for the live tiles.** A standard account gets about 2 Agent runs at a time. Ask the TinyFish booth for an increase first thing. If we don't get it: run TinyBrowser sessions (5) plus cached replays, and say in the pitch which tiles are live.
37	5. **Build order.** Core first, in this order: **robot CAD + bracket generator → agents find real motors → checks → regenerated bracket in the viewer.** Nothing else until that works end to end.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 4. Making the TinyFish part strong
42	
43	TinyFish judges on: **a real job done start to finish, agents that hold up on live websites, smart use of TinyFish, and a demo that makes them want to hire it.** The CAD step is what the job *produces*. It doesn't replace the job. Present it like a job description:
44	
45	> **Role:** Sourcing engineer. **Each run:** searches US motor manufacturers and distributors, reads product pages and datasheets, verifies origin and price from the source, and delivers specs that the CAD engine can build from.
46	
47	| Step | TinyFish product | What it does |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| Discovery | **TinySearch** + **TinyFetch** (free within limits) | Broad search across manufacturers and distributors for NEMA motors that meet the requirements. Cheap, so cast a wide net. |
50	| Deep extraction | **TinyAgent** (`/run-batch`, `/run-sse`) | Opens product pages, finds the datasheet, and returns the `output_schema` below. **Shows `streaming_url` tiles live on screen.** |
51	| Verification | **TinyFetch** (`html`) | Fetches the source page again and checks in code that `origin_quote`, the price and the frame size appear word for word. |
52	| Quote flow | **TinyBrowser** + Playwright | Fills one supplier's RFQ or quote form and **stops before submitting**. That's the end-to-end "job done." |
53	| Watching | **TinyMonitor** | Watches the chosen motor's page for price or stock changes. Events go to Tiger Data. |
54	
55	**Rules that make it hold up:**
56	- Every result carries `status` + `reason`. `COMPLETED` does not mean success.
57	- Data fields are optional, so unreachable fields don't get placeholder values.
58	- Use `max_duration_seconds` (GA) as the run limit. `max_steps` needs beta access.
59	- No CAPTCHA solving: mark the site `blocked` and move on. Test target sites in hour one.
60	- One honest identity on real sites. No fake personas.
61	- **Log every run to Tiger Data** (§8), then show a "success rate by site" panel. That's evidence the agents hold up on live websites, not just a claim.
62	- Pre-identify 2–3 real NEMA motors that the swarm is known to find, so the demo can't come up empty.
63	
64	**`output_schema` for the agent:**
65	
66	```json
67	{
68	  "status": "success | blocked | not_found | auth_required | incomplete",
69	  "reason": "string",
70	  "manufacturer": "string?",
71	  "part_number": "string?",
72	  "nema_frame": "string? (17 | 23 | 34)",
73	  "body_length_mm": "number?",
74	  "rated_torque_nm": "number?",
75	  "rated_speed_rpm": "number?",
76	  "voltage_v": "number?",
77	  "shaft_diameter_mm": "number?",
78	  "price_usd": "number?",
79	  "lead_time_days": "number?",
80	  "country_of_origin": "string?",
81	  "origin_quote": "string? (exact text from the page)",
82	  "product_url": "string?",
83	  "datasheet_url": "string?"
84	}
85	```
86	
87	**Social post (required for eligibility):** post the demo clip on X or LinkedIn and tag TinyFish.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 5. Pipeline: who does what
92	
93	| # | Step | Done by |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| 1 | Load the robot (parametric CadQuery model + BOM + requirements) | Code |
96	| 2 | Compliance card: coverage check, domestic %, US-assembly requirement, magnet supply-risk flag | Code |
97	| 3 | Plan the search: requirements → queries + target sites | Gemini |
98	| 4 | Discovery + extraction | TinyFish |
99	| 5 | Read datasheet PDFs where the page lacks specs | Gemini (multimodal, strict JSON) |
100	| 6 | Verify origin, price and frame size against the page HTML | Code |
101	| 7 | Engineering checks: torque, speed, voltage, fit | Code |
102	| 8 | Tournament: choose the best candidate by cost / performance / US-first | Code |
103	| 9 | Regenerate the bracket + assembly, export GLB | Code (CadQuery) |
104	| 10 | Explanations, comparison write-up, RFQ draft | Gemini (numbers passed in, no math) |
105	
106	**Hard rules:** the LLM never does arithmetic. Every number links to its source. Unverified candidates never reach the checks. "Not legal advice / not engineering certification" stays visible in the UI.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 6. Engineering checks (code)
111	
112	Inputs from the robot's spec: mass `m`, wheel radius `r`, number of drive motors `n`, gear ratio `G`, drivetrain efficiency `η`, rolling resistance `Crr`, maximum slope `θ`, target acceleration `a`, top speed `v_max`, bus voltage `V_bus`, safety factor `SF` (about 1.5).
113	
114	| Check | Pass if |
115	|---|---|
116	| Torque | `r·m·(g·(Crr·cosθ + sinθ) + a) / (n·G·η) · SF ≤ rated_torque_nm` |
117	| Speed | `(rated_speed_rpm / G) · 2πr / 60 ≥ v_max` |
118	| Voltage | `voltage_v` matches `V_bus` (or is within the driver's supported range) |
119	| Fit | `body_length_mm + bracket thickness + clearance ≤ chassis envelope`, and `nema_frame` is in the lookup table |
120	
121	Result per candidate: **Rejected** (fails torque, speed or voltage), **Review** (fits only with changes, or data is missing), **Pass\*** (meets every check we implemented).
122	
123	**NEMA lookup table.** These are typical values. **Check each one against a real vendor drawing before building**, because shaft size varies by model.
124	
125	| Frame | Bolt-hole spacing (square) | Pilot diameter | Common shaft diameter |
126	|---|---|---|---|
127	| NEMA 17 | 31.0 mm | 22.0 mm | 5 mm |
128	| NEMA 23 | 47.14 mm | 38.1 mm | 6.35 mm or 8 mm |
129	| NEMA 34 | 69.6 mm | 73.0 mm | 9.5 / 12.7 / 14 mm |
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 7. CAD engine
134	
135	- **CadQuery** (Python). Functions: `robot(params)`, `motor(frame, body_len)`, `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`.
136	- The bracket uses the bolt spacing and pilot diameter from the NEMA table, its width comes from the frame size, and its depth and position move with `body_len`.
137	- Export the assembly to **GLB** (glTF) for the browser, and to **STEP** as the "engineering export".
138	- Viewer: **`<model-viewer>`** or **three.js** with a **before/after slider**, the changed bracket highlighted, and the three tournament designs as tabs.
139	- **Start this first.** It's the least familiar piece and the biggest moment in the demo.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 8. Sponsor technology: how each one is used
144	
145	### TinyFish (core prize)
146	See §4. Search/Fetch for discovery, Agent for extraction with live tiles, Fetch HTML for verification, Browser for the RFQ form, Monitor for price and stock changes.
147	
148	### Gemini (MLH Best Use of Gemini)
149	- **Multimodal datasheet reading:** send PDFs or images of spec tables directly and get back **strict JSON** that matches our motor schema.
150	- **Long context:** compare 3–5 candidate datasheets side by side in one call and produce the spec comparison text.
151	- **Search planning:** robot requirements → search queries + target sites for TinyFish.
152	- **Writing:** fit explanations ("why Motor B needs review"), the design comparison write-up, and the RFQ draft.
153	- **Deliberately not used for:** arithmetic, pass/fail decisions, origin verification. Say this in the Devpost write-up.
154	
155	### Vultr (MLH Best Use of Vultr)
156	- **Backend on Vultr compute:** orchestrator API (FastAPI) + workers. Put CadQuery (OCCT dependencies) in a Docker image on the Vultr VM so nobody fights local installs.
157	- **Tournament in parallel:** each design variant is a worker job (checks + CAD regeneration + GLB export) running at the same time.
158	- **Vultr Object Storage** (S3-compatible): generated GLB/STEP files, downloaded datasheets, and captured HTML evidence for the verifier.
159	- Show the architecture diagram in the demo and name Vultr.
160	
161	### Tiger Data (MLH Best Use of Tiger Data)
162	Real time-series use, not just tables:
163	- **`agent_runs`** (hypertable): `time, run_id, site, product, status, duration_s, steps`. Continuous aggregate **`site_success_hourly`** powers the "success rate by site" panel. That panel doubles as TinyFish evidence.
164	- **`price_observations`** (hypertable): `time, part_number, supplier, price_usd, lead_time_days, origin, run_id`. Filled by repeated runs and TinyMonitor events.
165	- **`check_results`** (hypertable): `time, design_id, candidate, check, value, threshold, pass`. This is the audit trail behind each Pass/Review/Rejected.
166	- **`design_variants`** (regular table, same database): design ID, objective, cost, domestic %, GLB URL. Relational and time-series data side by side is Tiger Data's pitch.
167	- Name the hypertables and continuous aggregates in the Devpost write-up.
168	
169	### Also cheap to add (details in v1 §3a)
170	- **Auth0:** a manager approves before the RFQ is submitted.
171	- **Entire:** one Trail per feature plus session handoffs (see [ENTIRE.md](ENTIRE.md)).
172	- **GoDaddy:** a live domain hosting the demo.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 9. Demo script (3 minutes)
177	
178	1. **The problem (20 s):** the robot in 3D. "This drive motor has to go: here's the compliance card." It shows 38% domestic, needs US final assembly, and a separate magnet supply-risk flag.
179	2. **Find and Redesign (60 s):** click. Live TinyFish tiles search manufacturers and distributors, and verified results pop in (✅ / ⚠️ blocked / ❌ not found).
180	3. **Engineering checks (30 s):** the table shows Motor A Rejected (torque), Motor B Review (fit), Motor C Pass\*. Each number links to its source.
181	4. **The key moment (40 s):** the bracket regenerates. Before/after slider: the bracket widens and the holes move. STEP export button.
182	5. **Tournament (20 s):** three tabs (lowest cost / best performance / US-first), each with its cost, domestic %, and 3D model.
183	6. **Close (10 s):** RFQ drafted and waiting for approval. "From 'this part has to go' to a buildable design in 3 minutes."
184	
185	---
186	
187	## 10. Team split
188	
189	| Owner | Area |
190	|---|---|
191	| 1 | **CAD:** parametric robot + bracket in CadQuery, GLB/STEP export, 3D viewer with before/after |
192	| 2 | **Agents:** TinyFish discovery/extraction/verification, Gemini datasheet extraction, run logging |
193	| 3 | **Engineering + data:** checks, NEMA table, demo robot requirements, compliance card, 2–3 pre-identified real motors, Tiger Data schema |
194	| 4 | **Frontend + infra + demo:** UI flow, live tiles, comparison view, Vultr deployment, domain, video, social post |
195	
196	## 11. Milestones
197	
198	- [ ] **Now:** TinyFish booth (concurrency increase, beta access for `max_steps`, file upload). Ask the organizers about prize stacking. Test target sites for bot walls.
199	- [ ] **Sat 2pm:** a bracket regenerates from hard-coded motor specs and shows up in the viewer.
200	- [ ] **Sat 6pm:** the swarm returns verified specs for at least 2 real motors. The checks give Pass/Review/Rejected.
201	- [ ] **Sat 10pm:** end to end: click → agents → checks → regenerated bracket. Deployed on Vultr.
202	- [ ] **Sun 2am:** tournament (3 variants), Tiger Data panels, RFQ draft.
203	- [ ] **Sun 4am: FEATURE FREEZE.** 4–8am: pre-run and cache demo inputs, record a backup video, write the Devpost page, post the social clip.
204	
205	## 12. What to cut if we're behind (cut first at the top)
206	
207	1. Auth0 approval → show the RFQ as a draft only
208	2. TinyMonitor → static price history
209	3. Tournament → one redesign only
210	4. TinyBrowser quote form → link to the supplier's quote page
211	5. Tiger Data panels → a basic table (Tiger Data keeps logging in the background)
212	
213	**Never cut:** live agents finding real motors, code-based checks, the regenerated bracket in the viewer.
214

questions.question: Which frontend stack should the scaffold use? It needs a 3D viewer for the GLB models, live agent tiles and a comparison view.

options.label: Vite + React + TS (Recommended)
options.description: A static SPA that talks to FastAPI. It's the fastest to scaffold, the easiest to serve from Vultr or a domain, and uses react-three-fiber or <model-viewer> for the 3D viewer.

options.label: Next.js + TS
options.description: Gives you SSR/API routes, but the backend is already FastAPI, so those mostly add weight. Auth0 has a polished Next SDK.

options.label: Plain HTML + <model-viewer>
options.description: No build step, but it gets messy once you have tiles, tabs and a slider.

questions.question: How should the setup land in git? AGENTS.md says no AI co-author lines, and ENTIRE.md says one branch + Trail per feature.

options.label: Branch + Trail, then merge (Recommended)
options.description: Create a repo-setup branch and an Entire Trail, commit the scaffold, push the branch and let you merge. Teammates then branch per feature from main.

options.label: Commit straight to main
options.description: Fastest. Commit the scaffold to main and push, so all 4 owners can branch off right away.

options.label: Don't commit
options.description: Scaffold the files locally only. You review and push yourself.

# Plan: repo setup for AI Robot Redesign Engine

## Context
The repo only has docs right now: AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (untracked), HANDOFF(-v2).md and ENTIRE.md. Four owners (CAD, Agents, Engineering + data, Frontend + infra) need a skeleton they can each branch from. It should build and run on day one, with no keys in git, and follow the stack ARCHITECTURE.md already fixes: FastAPI orchestrator plus a CadQuery worker in Docker on Vultr, Tiger Data (Postgres/Timescale), Vultr Object Storage (S3), Gemini, TinyFish and Auth0. Frontend: **Vite + React + TS** (your choice). Git flow: **branch + Entire Trail, push, you merge** (your choice).

Toolchain on this machine: node 22, uv, python 3.12, entire. The existing .gitignore is GitHub's Python template, so it needs Node entries added.

## Layout (one folder per owner, filling in ARCHITECTURE.md §9)
```
backend/                      # uv project, Python 3.12, FastAPI
  pyproject.toml              # fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic-settings, httpx, psycopg[binary], boto3, google-genai; dev: pytest, ruff
  app/
    main.py                   # FastAPI app, CORS for the Vite dev origin, /health
    config.py                 # pydantic-settings Settings read from .env
    schemas.py                # Pydantic models from ARCHITECTURE §4: RobotRequirements, BomRow, MotorCandidate (output_schema), VerifierStatus, CheckResult, DesignVariant
    api/routes.py             # stub endpoints: GET /robot, GET /compliance, POST /runs (swarm), GET /designs
    agents/                   # Owner 2: swarm.py, verifier.py, datasheet.py, rfq.py  (stubs with docstrings)
    engineering/              # Owner 3: nema.py (NEMA lookup table, §5), checks.py (torque/speed/voltage/fit), compliance.py, tournament.py
    db/                       # tiger.py connection helper; storage.py S3 client for Vultr Object Storage
  tests/test_checks.py        # NEMA table + torque/speed formula smoke tests
cad/                          # Owner 1: separate image because of OCCT
  pyproject.toml              # cadquery, fastapi, uvicorn
  Dockerfile                  # python:3.12-slim + OCCT system libs + cadquery
  cad_worker/
    robot.py                  # robot(params), motor(frame, body_len), bracket(frame, body_len, clearance): stubs, bracket uses the NEMA table
    export.py                 # cq.Assembly -> GLB + STEP
    server.py                 # POST /build -> writes GLB/STEP (local dir or S3)
frontend/                     # Owner 4: npm create vite@latest -- --template react-ts
  src/api.ts                  # fetch wrapper using VITE_API_URL
  src/components/             # ComplianceCard, AgentTiles, ChecksTable, ModelViewer (<model-viewer>), DesignTabs: placeholders
  .env.example                # VITE_API_URL, VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN, VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID
db/
  schema.sql                  # Tiger Data: agent_runs, price_observations, check_results hypertables;
                              # site_success_hourly continuous aggregate; design_variants table (ARCH §4)
data/
  demo_robot.json             # demo requirements + BOM (placeholder values Owner 3 tunes)
  seed_motors.json            # slot for 2–3 pre-identified real motors (empty list + TODO)
docker-compose.yml            # backend, cad worker, local timescaledb (timescale/timescaledb image, runs db/schema.sql on init)
.env.example                  # GEMINI_API_KEY, TINYFISH_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, S3_ENDPOINT/S3_BUCKET/S3_ACCESS_KEY/S3_SECRET_KEY, AUTH0_DOMAIN/AUTH0_AUDIENCE, CAD_WORKER_URL. Names only, never values
Makefile                      # dev-backend, dev-cad, dev-frontend, up, test, lint
.editorconfig
.github/workflows/ci.yml      # ruff + pytest (backend), npm ci + build (frontend)
README.md                     # quickstart: copy .env, `make up`, `make dev-frontend`; links to docs
```
Other config:
- Add to `.gitignore`: `node_modules/`, `frontend/dist/`, `*.glb`, `*.step`, `cad/out/`, `.env.local`. (`.env` is already ignored.)
- Update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §9: replace the stub with this layout. Commit ARCHITECTURE.md, which is currently untracked.
- Rule 10 in ARCHITECTURE §6: secrets only go in `.env`, never in code, prompts or commits.

## Scope
Scaffolding only: typed schemas, the NEMA table and the check formulas from the docs (they're already fully specified, cheap to write and testable), plus stubs everything else can build on. No TinyFish, Gemini, Auth0 or Vultr integration logic yet. Those belong on each owner's feature branch.

## Git / push (per AGENTS.md + ENTIRE.md)
1. `git switch -c repo-setup`
2. `entire status` to check Entire is enabled. If it isn't, tell you to run `entire enable` / `entire login`, because a human has to finish the browser login.
3. `entire trail create --title "Repo setup: config, backend, frontend scaffold" --type feature`
4. Commit in logical chunks (config/tooling, backend, cad, frontend, db+data, docs). **No Co-Authored-By or AI footer lines**, per AGENTS.md, which overrides the default.
5. Run `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` to check there are no secrets in the transcripts, then `git push -u origin repo-setup`.
6. Leave the merge to you (or `entire trail ready` / `entire trail merge` once you approve).

## Verification
- `cd backend && uv sync && uv run pytest && uv run ruff check .`
- `uv run uvicorn app.main:app` → `curl localhost:8000/health` returns ok
- `cd frontend && npm install && npm run build`; `npm run dev` loads and calls /health
- `docker compose config` validates. `docker compose up db` applies schema.sql (only if Docker is available in WSL; otherwise I'll say so)
- `docker build cad/` if Docker is available. The CadQuery image is heavy, so I'll report it if it's skipped.
- `git grep -iE 'api[_-]?key\s*=\s*\S{8,}'` finds no real secrets

"""Deterministic engineering checks (ARCHITECTURE §5). The LLM never does this arithmetic.

Owner 3 owns thresholds, fit-badge rules and the spec comparison table.
"""

import math

from app.engineering.nema import lookup
from app.schemas import CheckResult, CheckRow, Fit, MotorCandidate, RobotRequirements, Verdict

G = 9.81
BRACKET_THICKNESS_MM = 5.0  # TODO(owner 3): take from the CAD bracket params
CLEARANCE_MM = 5.0


def required_torque_nm(req: RobotRequirements) -> float:
    """r·m·(g·(Crr·cosθ + sinθ) + a) / (n·G·η) · SF — required torque per motor."""
    theta = math.radians(req.max_slope_deg)
    force = req.mass_kg * (G * (req.crr * math.cos(theta) + math.sin(theta)) + req.accel_mps2)
    wheel_torque = req.wheel_radius_m * force
    return wheel_torque / (req.n_drive_motors * req.gear_ratio * req.efficiency) * req.safety_factor


def top_speed_mps(rated_speed_rpm: float, req: RobotRequirements) -> float:
    """(rated_speed_rpm / G) · 2πr / 60."""
    return (rated_speed_rpm / req.gear_ratio) * 2 * math.pi * req.wheel_radius_m / 60


def run_checks(motor: MotorCandidate, req: RobotRequirements) -> CheckResult:
    sources = [u for u in (motor.product_url, motor.datasheet_url) if u]
    rows: list[CheckRow] = []

    need_t = required_torque_nm(req)
    t = motor.rated_torque_nm
    rows.append(CheckRow(check="torque", value=t, threshold=need_t,
                         passed=None if t is None else t >= need_t, sources=sources))

    v = None if motor.rated_speed_rpm is None else top_speed_mps(motor.rated_speed_rpm, req)
    rows.append(CheckRow(check="speed", value=v, threshold=req.v_max_mps,
                         passed=None if v is None else v >= req.v_max_mps, sources=sources))

    # TODO(owner 3): accept a driver-supported voltage range instead of exact match.
    volt = motor.voltage_v
    rows.append(CheckRow(check="voltage", value=volt, threshold=req.bus_voltage_v,
                         passed=None if volt is None else math.isclose(volt, req.bus_voltage_v),
                         sources=sources))

    frame = lookup(motor.nema_frame)
    length = motor.body_length_mm
    fit_len = None if length is None else length + BRACKET_THICKNESS_MM + CLEARANCE_MM
    fit_ok = None if fit_len is None or frame is None else fit_len <= req.envelope_mm
    rows.append(CheckRow(check="fit", value=fit_len, threshold=req.envelope_mm,
                         passed=fit_ok, sources=sources))

    hard = {r.check: r.passed for r in rows}
    if any(hard[c] is False for c in ("torque", "speed", "voltage")):
        verdict = Verdict.rejected
    elif all(r.passed for r in rows):
        verdict = Verdict.passed
    else:
        verdict = Verdict.review

    # TODO(owner 3): real drop_in/close rule (same frame as current motor, length delta).
    fit = Fit.drop_in if fit_ok else Fit.needs_review
    return CheckResult(candidate=motor.part_number or "unknown", verdict=verdict, fit=fit, rows=rows)

"""Compliance card (ARCHITECTURE §3 #2, §6 rules 3–5). Deterministic.

Compliance and supply risk are separate tracks. Unknown origin and allied (e.g. CA) parts
count as foreign. A domestic end product also needs US final assembly.
"""

from decimal import Decimal

from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.schemas import Robot

THRESHOLDS_PCT = (65, 75)


class ComplianceCard(BaseModel):
    domestic_pct: float
    thresholds_pct: tuple[int, ...] = THRESHOLDS_PCT
    us_final_assembly: bool
    supply_risks: list[str]
    notes: list[str]


def compliance_card(robot: Robot) -> ComplianceCard:
    total = sum((r.unit_cost_usd * r.qty for r in robot.bom), Decimal(0))
    domestic = sum(
        (r.unit_cost_usd * r.qty for r in robot.bom if r.origin.upper() == "US"), Decimal(0)
    )
    pct = float(domestic / total * 100) if total else 0.0
    us_assembly = robot.final_assembly_country.upper() == "US"

    notes = ["Not legal advice. COTS treatment: flag for counsel."]
    if not us_assembly:
        notes.append("Also needs US final assembly to be a domestic end product.")

    risks = sorted({f"{r.part}: {r.supply_risk}" for r in robot.bom if r.supply_risk})
    # TODO(owner 3): FCC coverage check.
    return ComplianceCard(domestic_pct=round(pct, 1), us_final_assembly=us_assembly,
                          supply_risks=risks, notes=notes)

"""Parametric robot (ARCHITECTURE §5). Owner 1.

Clean and labelled beats realistic. Only the motor bracket changes between designs.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

import cadquery as cq

from cad_worker.nema import BOLT_HOLE_MM, NEMA

BRACKET_THICKNESS = 5.0


@dataclass
class RobotParams:
    frame: str = "23"
    body_len: float = 56.0
    clearance: float = 5.0
    plate_l: float = 300.0
    plate_w: float = 220.0
    plate_t: float = 6.0
    wheel_r: float = 50.0
    wheel_w: float = 25.0


def motor(frame: str, body_len: float) -> cq.Workplane:
    _, pilot, face = NEMA[frame]
    body = cq.Workplane("YZ").rect(face, face).extrude(body_len)
    boss = cq.Workplane("YZ").circle(pilot / 2).extrude(-2.0)
    return body.union(boss)


def bracket(frame: str, body_len: float, clearance: float) -> cq.Workplane:
    """L-bracket: vertical face with NEMA bolt pattern + pilot hole, horizontal foot."""
    spacing, pilot, face = NEMA[frame]
    width = face + 10
    height = face + 10
    foot = body_len + clearance
    plate = (
        cq.Workplane("YZ")
        .rect(width, height)
        .extrude(BRACKET_THICKNESS)
        .faces(">X")
        .workplane()
        .hole(pilot + 1.0)
        .faces(">X")
        .workplane()
        .rect(spacing, spacing, forConstruction=True)
        .vertices()
        .hole(BOLT_HOLE_MM[frame])
    )
    base = (
        cq.Workplane("XY")
        .box(foot, width, BRACKET_THICKNESS, centered=(False, True, False))
        .translate((-foot, 0, -height / 2))
    )
    return plate.union(base)


def robot(p: RobotParams) -> cq.Assembly:
    face = NEMA[p.frame][2]
    z_axis = p.plate_t + (face + 10) / 2  # motor axis height above the plate's bottom
    assy = cq.Assembly(name="robot")
    assy.add(
        cq.Workplane("XY").box(p.plate_l, p.plate_w, p.plate_t, centered=(True, True, False)),
        name="base_plate",
        color=cq.Color("gray"),
    )
    assy.add(
        cq.Workplane("XY").box(120, 80, 50, centered=(True, True, False)).translate((40, 0, p.plate_t)),
        name="electronics_box",
        color=cq.Color("black"),
    )
    for side, y in (("left", 1), ("right", -1)):
        y_mount = y * (p.plate_w / 2 - face / 2 - 10)
        loc = cq.Location(cq.Vector(-p.plate_l / 2 + 40, y_mount, z_axis))
        rot = cq.Location(cq.Vector(0, 0, 0), cq.Vector(0, 0, 1), 90 * y)
        assy.add(
            bracket(p.frame, p.body_len, p.clearance),
            name=f"bracket_{side}",
            loc=loc * rot,
            color=cq.Color("orange"),
        )
        assy.add(
            motor(p.frame, p.body_len).translate((-p.body_len - BRACKET_THICKNESS, 0, 0)),
            name=f"motor_{side}",
            loc=loc * rot * cq.Location(cq.Vector(BRACKET_THICKNESS, 0, 0)),
            color=cq.Color("blue"),
        )
        wheel = cq.Workplane("XZ").circle(p.wheel_r).extrude(p.wheel_w / 2, both=True)
        assy.add(
            wheel,
            name=f"wheel_{side}",
            loc=cq.Location(cq.Vector(-p.plate_l / 2 + 40, y * (p.plate_w / 2 + p.wheel_w), p.wheel_r)),
            color=cq.Color("black"),
        )
    return assy

mkdir -p db && cat > db/schema.sql <<'EOF'
-- Tiger Data schema (ARCHITECTURE §4). Runs on Tiger Cloud or the local timescaledb container.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;

-- One row per TinyFish agent run. Evidence that the agents hold up on live sites.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_runs (
  time        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  run_id      TEXT        NOT NULL,
  site        TEXT        NOT NULL,
  product     TEXT,
  status      TEXT        NOT NULL,  -- success | blocked | not_found | auth_required | incomplete
  duration_s  DOUBLE PRECISION,
  steps       INTEGER
);
SELECT create_hypertable('agent_runs', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS site_success_hourly
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', time) AS bucket,
       site,
       count(*)                                   AS runs,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') AS successes
FROM agent_runs
GROUP BY bucket, site
WITH NO DATA;

SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('site_success_hourly',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '1 day', end_offset => NULL,
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '5 minutes', if_not_exists => TRUE);

-- Price/lead-time history from repeated runs and TinyMonitor events.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS price_observations (
  time            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  part_number     TEXT        NOT NULL,
  supplier        TEXT        NOT NULL,
  price_usd       NUMERIC(12,2),
  lead_time_days  DOUBLE PRECISION,
  origin          TEXT,
  run_id          TEXT
);
SELECT create_hypertable('price_observations', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);

-- Audit trail behind each Pass / Review / Rejected.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS check_results (
  time       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  design_id  TEXT        NOT NULL,
  candidate  TEXT        NOT NULL,
  "check"    TEXT        NOT NULL,
  value      DOUBLE PRECISION,
  threshold  DOUBLE PRECISION,
  pass       BOOLEAN
);
SELECT create_hypertable('check_results', by_range('time'), if_not_exists => TRUE);

-- Relational table alongside the hypertables.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS design_variants (
  design_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  objective     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (objective IN ('cost', 'performance', 'us_first')),
  motor         TEXT NOT NULL,
  cost_usd      NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  domestic_pct  DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
  glb_url       TEXT,
  step_url      TEXT,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
EOF
cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'
# Local stack. On Vultr, point DATABASE_URL at Tiger Cloud and drop the db service.
services:
  db:
    image: timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: REDACTED
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
      POSTGRES_DB: redesign
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    volumes:
      - ./db/schema.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/01-schema.sql:ro
      - dbdata:/var/lib/REDACTEDql/data

  cad:
    build: ./cad
    ports: ["8001:8001"]
    volumes:
      - ./cad/out:/app/out

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
      CAD_WORKER_URL: http://cad:8001
      DATA_DIR: /data
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data:ro
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
    depends_on: [db, cad]

volumes:
  dbdata:
EOF

# AI Robot Redesign Engine (Hack Western 13)

Tell it a robot's drive motor has to be replaced to meet US sourcing rules. TinyFish agents find real NEMA replacement motors and verify them on the vendors' sites. Code checks the engineering, and CadQuery regenerates the motor bracket to fit the new motor.

- Plan, demo script and team split: [docs/HANDOFF-v2.md](docs/HANDOFF-v2.md)
- Architecture, schemas and repo layout: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- Entire workflow (branch + Trail per feature): [docs/ENTIRE.md](docs/ENTIRE.md)
- Agent rules: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)

## Prerequisites

Node 22, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Docker. You don't need CadQuery or OCCT locally because they only run in Docker.

## Quickstart

```bash
cp .env.example .env              # fill in keys; never commit .env or paste keys into prompts
make install                      # backend (uv) + frontend (npm) deps
make db                           # local TimescaleDB with db/schema.sql applied
docker compose up -d --build cad  # CAD worker on :8001
make dev-backend                  # FastAPI on :8000  (docs at /docs)
make dev-frontend                 # Vite on :5173, proxies /api to :8000 and /cad to :8001
```

Make a sample model for the viewer:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8001/build -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"design_id":"test_23"}'
```

`make test` runs the backend tests. `make lint` runs ruff and oxlint. `make up` runs the full stack in Docker.

If ROS (or anything else) sets `PYTHONPATH` in your shell, use the `make` targets, which unset it. Otherwise pytest loads foreign plugins.

## Working on a feature

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c <feature-branch>
entire trail create --title "<feature>" --type feature
```

Commits must not credit any AI as an author (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)).

The repo is scaffolded and pushed to the `repo-setup` branch. It's linked to [Entire Trail #1](https://entire.com/gh/kingsolima/-/trails/1), and I haven't merged it, so that's yours to do.

**What's in it** (six commits, with no AI co-author lines as AGENTS.md requires):
- **Config:** a `.env.example` listing the variable names with no values, a `Makefile` with `install`/`dev-*`/`test`/`lint`/`up`, a GitHub Actions CI workflow, `.editorconfig`, and Node and CAD-output entries added to `.gitignore`.
- **Backend** ([backend/](backend/)): a FastAPI app managed with uv. [schemas.py](backend/app/schemas.py) mirrors the data contracts in ARCHITECTURE §4. The NEMA table, the four engineering checks and the compliance card are real code with 7 passing tests. The agent swarm, verifier, datasheet reader, RFQ flow and tournament are stubs for each owner to fill in.
- **CAD worker** ([cad/](cad/)): a Docker image with a working `robot()`, `motor()` and `bracket()`. `POST /build` produces GLB and STEP files.
- **Frontend** ([frontend/](frontend/)): Vite + React + TypeScript with an API client, types and placeholder panels: the compliance card, agent tiles, checks table, a 3D viewer using `<model-viewer>`, and design tabs.
- **Data:** [db/schema.sql](db/schema.sql) for Tiger Data, [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) for the local stack, and [data/demo_robot.json](data/demo_robot.json), a demo robot that comes out at 37.9% domestic and needs US final assembly.
- **Docs:** a README quickstart, and ARCHITECTURE.md §9 now describes the actual layout.

**What I tested:**
- Backend lint and tests pass, and the frontend builds and lints clean.
- The schema applies in TimescaleDB: 3 hypertables, `site_success_hourly` and `design_variants`.
- The CAD image builds GLB and STEP files for NEMA 17, 23 and 34.
- The full loop works through the Vite proxy: health, compliance card, checks, a CAD build, and the GLB served back.
- The backend image builds.

**Things you should know:**
- **I ran `entire enable` in this clone.** It wasn't set up yet, and I turned telemetry off. That added `.claude/settings.json` and `.entire/` to the first commit.
- **The repo is public, so the pushed session transcripts are public.** One of the 5 uploaded checkpoints came from another session (the prompt starts "look at handoffv2…"). I scanned all 5 and found no keys or emails.
- **I didn't commit `docs/HANDOFF-v2.md`.** It has 44 lines of changes I didn't make.
- **I haven't looked at the 3D model.** The files build and export, but the bracket and motor positions in the robot assembly may need adjusting by the CAD owner.
- **`data/seed_motors.json` is empty on purpose.** The engineering owner needs to add 2–3 real motors rather than invented specs.
- **Your shell's ROS `PYTHONPATH` breaks pytest.** The `make` targets unset it; running `uv run pytest` directly needs `PYTHONPATH=` in front.
- **A few things are still running or left behind:** the local `db` container is stopped but its volume is still there, and there are test GLB files in `cad/out/`. Those files are owned by root and gitignored.

Yes, you need one Docker container: the CAD worker. The backend and frontend run straight from your terminal. Use three terminals, all from the repo root.

**Terminal 1: CAD worker (Docker)**
```bash
make dev-cad
```
This builds and runs the CadQuery container on port 8001 in the foreground. Leave it running.

**Terminal 2: backend (no Docker)**
```bash
make dev-backend
```
FastAPI runs on port 8000. The page works without it, but you'd lose the compliance card and checks panels.

**Terminal 3: frontend**
```bash
make dev-frontend
```

**Generate a model and look at it.** In any spare terminal:
```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8001/build -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"design_id":"test_23"}'
```
Then open http://localhost:5173. The viewer loads `test_23.glb`, the name [App.tsx](frontend/src/App.tsx) currently hardcodes. Drag to rotate.

To compare frames, build the other two and temporarily change that `src` in App.tsx:

You're running three separate programs that talk to each other. The curl command is how you trigger one of them by hand, because the button that will eventually do it hasn't been built yet.

**The three programs**

| Program | Port | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **CAD worker** (Docker) | 8001 | Draws the robot in 3D. You send it motor details, such as "NEMA 23, 56 mm long", and it writes a 3D model file (`.glb`) sized to fit that motor. |
| **Backend** | 8000 | The "brain": compliance %, the engineering checks, and later the TinyFish agents. It answers questions from the website. |
| **Frontend** | 5173 | The website you open in your browser. It displays whatever the other two produce. |

The CAD worker runs in Docker only because CadQuery is painful to install locally. Docker gives it a ready-made environment.

**What the curl does**

The CAD worker only draws something when it's asked. This command:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8001/build -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"design_id":"test_23"}'
```

means: "CAD worker, build the robot with the default motor (NEMA 23) and save it as `test_23.glb`." Its reply tells you where the file was saved.

The website is currently hardcoded to show `test_23.glb`. Without that curl, the viewer has nothing to display.

1. The user clicks **Find and Redesign** on the website.
2. The backend sends agents to find real motors, checks them, and picks a winner.
3. The backend asks the CAD worker to build a robot around that motor. This is the same request as your curl, sent automatically.
4. The website shows the new model.

"""Parametric robot (ARCHITECTURE §5). Owner 1.

Clean and labelled beats realistic. Only the motor bracket changes between designs.

World frame: X forward, Y left, Z up, ground at z=0. The robot is a differential drive:
two direct-drive wheels on a rear axle plus a front caster. Each motor's shaft points
outward along Y, straight into its wheel's hub, so the motor axis height equals the
wheel radius.

Parts are built in a per-side local frame: motor axis along +Y (towards the wheel),
x=0 and z=0 on the motor axis, y=0 at the motor's mounting face. The right side is
the left side rotated 180° about Z.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

import cadquery as cq

from cad_worker.nema import BOLT_HOLE_MM, NEMA, SHAFT_MM

BRACKET_T = 5.0  # bracket plate thickness
BRACKET_MARGIN = 5.0  # bracket material around the motor face
EDGE_INSET = 5.0  # bracket outer face inset from the base plate's edge


@dataclass
class RobotParams:
    frame: str = "23"
    body_len: float = 56.0
    clearance: float = 5.0
    plate_l: float = 300.0
    plate_w: float = 220.0
    plate_t: float = 6.0
    ground_clearance: float = 10.0  # floor to the underside of the plate
    wheel_r: float = 70.0  # big enough that a NEMA 34 still clears the plate
    wheel_w: float = 25.0
    wheel_gap: float = 10.0  # plate edge to the wheel's inner face
    axle_from_rear: float = 70.0


def _cylinder(r: float, length: float, start, direction=(0, 1, 0)) -> cq.Workplane:
    solid = cq.Solid.makeCylinder(r, length, cq.Vector(*start), cq.Vector(*direction))
    return cq.Workplane("XY").add(solid)


def _box(dx: float, dy: float, dz: float, center) -> cq.Workplane:
    return cq.Workplane("XY").box(dx, dy, dz).translate(center)


def motor(frame: str, body_len: float) -> cq.Workplane:
    """NEMA motor body in the local frame: face at y=0, body towards -Y, pilot boss to +Y."""
    _, pilot, face = NEMA[frame]
    body = _box(face, body_len, face, (0, -body_len / 2, 0))
    boss = _cylinder(pilot / 2, 2.0, (0, 0, 0))
    return body.union(boss)


def shaft(frame: str, length: float) -> cq.Workplane:
    return _cylinder(SHAFT_MM[frame] / 2, length, (0, 0, 0))


def bracket(
    frame: str, body_len: float, clearance: float, axis_height: float | None = None
) -> cq.Workplane:
    """L-bracket in the local frame.

    The upright (y in [0, T]) carries the NEMA bolt square and pilot hole on the motor
    axis, `axis_height` above the plate's top surface. The foot lies flat on the plate
    and runs inboard under the motor body; its depth follows `body_len`.
    Bolt spacing and pilot diameter come from the NEMA table, never from a datasheet.
    """
    spacing, pilot, face = NEMA[frame]
    if axis_height is None:
        axis_height = face / 2 + BRACKET_T
    width = face + 2 * BRACKET_MARGIN
    height = axis_height + face / 2 + BRACKET_MARGIN
    upright = _box(width, BRACKET_T, height, (0, BRACKET_T / 2, -axis_height + height / 2))

    foot_len = body_len + clearance + BRACKET_T
    foot = _box(
        width, foot_len, BRACKET_T,
        (0, BRACKET_T - foot_len / 2, -axis_height + BRACKET_T / 2),
    )

    body = upright.union(foot)
    body = body.cut(_cylinder((pilot + 1.0) / 2, BRACKET_T + 2, (0, -1, 0)))
    r = BOLT_HOLE_MM[frame] / 2
    for dx in (-spacing / 2, spacing / 2):
        for dz in (-spacing / 2, spacing / 2):
            body = body.cut(_cylinder(r, BRACKET_T + 2, (dx, -1, dz)))
    return body


def robot(p: RobotParams) -> cq.Assembly:
    face = NEMA[p.frame][2]
    plate_top = p.ground_clearance + p.plate_t
    axle_z = p.wheel_r  # wheels touch the ground
    axis_height = axle_z - plate_top
    if axis_height - BRACKET_T < face / 2:
        raise ValueError(f"NEMA {p.frame} does not clear the plate with wheel_r={p.wheel_r}")

    axle_x = -p.plate_l / 2 + p.axle_from_rear
    motor_face_y = p.plate_w / 2 - EDGE_INSET - BRACKET_T  # inner face of the bracket
    wheel_center_y = p.plate_w / 2 + p.wheel_gap + p.wheel_w / 2

    assy = cq.Assembly(name="robot")
    assy.add(
        _box(p.plate_l, p.plate_w, p.plate_t, (0, 0, p.ground_clearance + p.plate_t / 2)),
        name="base_plate",
        color=cq.Color("gray"),
    )
    assy.add(
        _box(120, 80, 50, (40, 0, plate_top + 25)),
        name="electronics_box",
        color=cq.Color("black"),
    )
    caster_r = p.ground_clearance
    assy.add(
        cq.Workplane("XY").sphere(caster_r).translate((p.plate_l / 2 - 30, 0, caster_r)),
        name="caster",
        color=cq.Color(0.75, 0.75, 0.75),
    )

    for side, angle in (("left", 0), ("right", 180)):
        loc = cq.Location(cq.Vector(axle_x, 0, axle_z)) * cq.Location(
            cq.Vector(0, 0, 0), cq.Vector(0, 0, 1), angle
        )
        assy.add(
            bracket(p.frame, p.body_len, p.clearance, axis_height).translate((0, motor_face_y, 0)),
            name=f"bracket_{side}",
            loc=loc,
            color=cq.Color("orange"),
        )
        assy.add(
            motor(p.frame, p.body_len).translate((0, motor_face_y, 0)),
            name=f"motor_{side}",
            loc=loc,
            color=cq.Color("blue"),
        )
        assy.add(
            shaft(p.frame, wheel_center_y - motor_face_y).translate((0, motor_face_y, 0)),
            name=f"shaft_{side}",
            loc=loc,
            color=cq.Color(0.75, 0.75, 0.75),
        )
        assy.add(
            _cylinder(p.wheel_r, p.wheel_w, (0, wheel_center_y - p.wheel_w / 2, 0)),
            name=f"wheel_{side}",
            loc=loc,
            color=cq.Color(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
        )
    return assy

I fixed all three placement problems, and the robot now sits on its wheels the way a real one would. The new 3D files are already on disk, so refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R) to see them.

**What changed** in [robot.py](cad/cad_worker/robot.py):

3. **Each motor sits next to its own wheel**, near the back of the robot.

**The bracket now changes visibly with the motor.** Bigger motors get a taller, wider bracket, and longer motors get a longer bracket base. That's what you'll show when the motor gets swapped.

**How I checked it:** I measured the model for NEMA 17, 23 and 34. In all three, the bottom of the robot is at floor level, each shaft is at the same height as the wheel centers (70 mm up), and each shaft ends at the middle of its wheel. I also rendered front and top views, but I haven't seen it in your browser, so let me know if anything looks off.

- The CAD worker in terminal 1 is still running the old code. Restart it (Ctrl+C, then `make dev-cad`) before you run any new curl, or you'll get the old robot back.

**How v3 changes the plan**

v3 replaces the next steps I gave you. The main differences:

- **More than one motor search.** An orchestrator runs one worker per BOM line. A swap worker hunts for replacement drive motors, and 2–3 origin workers try to prove where expensive parts like the battery and compute board are made.

- **Record/replay from the start.** Every TinyFish and Gemini call can be saved and replayed, so the demo works even if live sites fail. The UI shows a LIVE or REPLAY badge.
- **A synthesis step.** Three "advocates" (cost, performance, US-first) argue their case, a writer summarizes, and a Gemini critic can send back one round of follow-up questions. LLMs still never produce numbers or verdicts.

If 60 mm wheels means 60 mm diameter, the motor shaft sits only 30 mm off the ground, and even a NEMA 23 hits the floor. I checked the design docs, and I need to correct one thing I said earlier. The 60 mm is the wheel **radius**, not the diameter (03-v2-review says "r = 60 mm"), so NEMA 23 does fit. The real CAD problem is NEMA 34.

**Before (main) vs after (v3)**

| Area | Before (what's on main) | After (v3) |
|---|---|---|
| **Demo robot** | 8 kg, belt drive (G = 3), 70 mm wheel radius | ~5 kg, direct drive (G = 1), 60 mm wheel radius |
| **Motor data** | One flat record per motor: `rated_torque_nm`, `voltage_v`, `price_usd`… | Each spec is a separate **Claim** with the value and unit as written, the exact quote and the source URL. A spec only counts once the verifier confirms the quote is on the page. |
| **Motor type** | Not tracked | `servo_integrated`, `bldc`, `stepper` or `brushed_dc`. The rules differ per type, and steppers are capped at Review. |
| **Checks** | 4 checks: torque, speed, exact voltage match, length fit | 7 checks: continuous torque, peak torque, speed, voltage range, envelope fit, **ground clearance** and **shaft-vs-wheel-bore**. Real drop_in/close badge. |
| **Compliance** | Domestic % by unit cost, origin is a plain country code | Domestic % by **landed cost** (price + freight + duty), only origin tiers T1/T2 count as US, must be strictly above 65%, and the COTS note is replaced |
| **Agents** | One `find_candidates()` stub | An orchestrator plus swap and origin workers, record/replay, and the synthesis step |
| **Database** | 3 hypertables, one aggregate, `design_variants` | Adds `board` (the blackboard) and `tasks`, plus new columns on `agent_runs` and `price_observations`, and a `supplier_1h` aggregate |
| **API** | `GET /api/robot`, `/api/compliance`, `POST /api/checks`, `/api/runs` (stub) | `POST /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `GET /jobs/{id}/events` (live updates over SSE), `GET /designs/{id}/glb` and `/step` |

**What breaks when you apply v3**

1. **The motor schema change breaks four places.** `checks.py`, the `/api/checks` route, `frontend/src/types.ts` and the backend tests all read flat fields like `motor.rated_torque_nm`. They have to change together in one commit, or the tests and the frontend checks table stop working.
2. **The CAD model rejects NEMA 34.** With a 60 mm wheel radius, the motor shaft sits 44 mm above the plate, but a NEMA 34 needs 48 mm, so `robot()` raises an error instead of building. NEMA 17 and 23 still work. This is v3's known issue ("NEMA 34 leaves about 4 mm"). The fix is to make NEMA 34 fail the new ground-clearance check instead of crashing, or to lower the plate.
3. **The requirement field names conflict.** 04-architecture renames fields (`n_drive_motors` to `n_drive`, `efficiency` to `eta`, `bus_voltage_v` to `v_bus`, `envelope_mm` to `inboard_room_mm`), but HANDOFF-v3 §4 says keep the existing names and only add new ones. Pick one before Owners 2 and 3 both edit `schemas.py`. I'd keep the existing names, since §4 is the newer instruction.
4. **The frontend's API calls go stale.** `api.ts` calls `/api/...`; v3 uses `/jobs` with SSE events. The current panels keep working until the old routes are removed.
5. **The demo numbers change.** `demo_robot.json` needs the new robot and a BOM with real prices, origins, freight and duty, so the 37.9% domestic figure will change.

**What doesn't break**
- **The database schema.** v3 worries the `FILTER` clause might fail, but we already ran it on TimescaleDB today and it worked. v3 adds tables and columns rather than replacing them.
- **Docker, CI, the Makefile and the Entire setup.**
- **The bracket code**, including the NEMA table, which v3 says is better than its own CAD spike.

The safest order is: first agree on the field names (3), then make one commit that changes the schema, checks, tests and frontend types together (1). Do you want me to do that on a branch?

A COMPLETED status does not mean the goal succeeded.

"""TinyAgent output_schema for a motor candidate (HANDOFF-v3 §3 contract).

The JSON file in docs/design/schemas is the source of truth; the Pydantic models mirror it to
validate what the agent returns. Change both together and tell the other owners.
"""

import json
from functools import cache
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.config import REPO_ROOT

SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "design" / "schemas" / "motor_candidate.tinyfish.json"

SpecName = Literal[
    "continuous_torque", "peak_torque", "holding_torque", "torque_at_speed",
    "rated_speed", "max_speed",
    "supply_voltage_min", "supply_voltage_max", "rated_voltage", "rated_current",
    "body_length", "shaft_diameter", "price", "lead_time",
]  # fmt: skip


@cache
def output_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text())


class TfSpec(BaseModel):
    name: SpecName
    value: float
    unit: str
    at_speed_value: float | None
    at_speed_unit: str | None
    quote: str
    source_url: str


class TfMotorCandidate(BaseModel):
    status: Literal["success", "blocked", "not_found", "auth_required", "incomplete"]
    reason: str
    manufacturer: str | None
    part_number: str | None
    motor_type: Literal["servo_integrated", "bldc", "stepper", "brushed_dc", "unknown"] | None
    nema_frame: Literal["17", "23", "34", "other"] | None
    specs: list[TfSpec]
    country_of_origin: str | None
    origin_quote: str | None
    origin_source_url: str | None
    product_url: str | None
    datasheet_url: str | None

"""Known-good demo target: Teknic ClearPath-SD (HANDOFF-v3 §10).

The family page has no per-model specs; they sit on model pages behind the model list, and
the manufacturing claim is on another page. That makes it a real multi-page TinyAgent job.
"""

TEKNIC_URL = "https://teknic.com/products/clearpath-brushless-dc-servo-motors/clearpath-sd/"


def build_goal() -> str:
    return """\
You are a sourcing engineer collecting verifiable specs for ONE motor. Do not buy, log in, \
fill forms or sign up for anything.

1. On this Teknic ClearPath-SD page, go to the list of ClearPath-SD models \
("All ClearPath models", filtered to SDSK if possible).
2. Pick ONE NEMA 23 SDSK model (part number starts with CPM-SDSK-23) and open its \
specification / model information page.
3. From that model's page, fill `specs` with every one of these that is shown: \
continuous_torque, peak_torque, max_speed, supply_voltage_min, supply_voltage_max, \
body_length, shaft_diameter, price. For each spec:
   - value = the number exactly as shown, unit = the unit exactly as shown (e.g. "oz-in", \
"N-m", "RPM", "VDC", "in", "mm", "USD"); do not convert units.
   - quote = the exact text copied from the page that contains that number (a short \
label + value), character for character.
   - source_url = the URL of the page where you read it.
   - at_speed_value / at_speed_unit only if the page ties the torque to a speed, else null.
4. Find where Teknic states ClearPath motors are manufactured (try the model page, then the \
About page). Put the exact sentence in origin_quote, its page URL in origin_source_url, and \
the country it names in country_of_origin. "Designed in" or a headquarters address is NOT \
a manufacturing statement: leave origin fields null in that case.
5. manufacturer = "Teknic", part_number = the model's part number, motor_type = \
"servo_integrated", nema_frame = "23", product_url = the model page URL, datasheet_url = a \
manual/datasheet PDF link if one is on the model page, else null.

Rules: never guess or fill placeholders; use null (or omit a spec) when not shown. \
If a CAPTCHA, bot check or access-denied page blocks you, return status "blocked" with the \
reason. If you cannot find any NEMA 23 SDSK model, return status "not_found". If some fields \
are missing, return status "incomplete" and list what is missing in reason. Otherwise status \
"success".
"""

A live run costs TinyFish agent credit. Open the printed streaming URL to watch it.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from pydantic import ValidationError  # noqa: E402

from app.agents.motor_schema import TfMotorCandidate, output_schema  # noqa: E402
from app.agents.teknic import TEKNIC_URL, build_goal  # noqa: E402
from app.tfclient.client import TinyFishClient  # noqa: E402


async def main(live: bool, max_duration: int) -> int:
    client = TinyFishClient("live" if live else "replay")
    print(f"mode: {client.mode} | url: {TEKNIC_URL}")
    complete = None
    async for ev in client.agent_run_sse(
        TEKNIC_URL, build_goal(), output_schema(), max_duration_seconds=max_duration
    ):
        t = ev.get("type")
        if t == "STARTED":
            print(f"run started: {ev.get('run_id')}")
        elif t == "STREAMING_URL":
            print(f"watch live: {ev.get('streaming_url')}")
        elif t == "PROGRESS":
            print(f"  · {ev.get('purpose')}")
        elif t == "COMPLETE":
            complete = ev
        sys.stdout.flush()

    if complete is None:
        print("stream ended without COMPLETE; check the run with GET /v1/runs/{run_id}")
        return 1
    print(f"\nrun status: {complete.get('status')}  (COMPLETED does not mean success)")
    if complete.get("error"):
        print(f"error: {complete['error']}")
    result = complete.get("result")
    if not isinstance(result, dict):
        print(f"no structured result: {result!r}")
        return 1
    try:
        cand = TfMotorCandidate.model_validate(result)
    except ValidationError as e:
        print(f"result does not match the schema:\n{e}\nraw: {result}")
        return 1

    print(f"agent status: {cand.status} — {cand.reason}")
    print(f"{cand.manufacturer} {cand.part_number} | {cand.motor_type} | NEMA {cand.nema_frame}")
    print(f"product: {cand.product_url}\ndatasheet: {cand.datasheet_url}\n")
    for s in cand.specs:
        at = f" @ {s.at_speed_value} {s.at_speed_unit}" if s.at_speed_value is not None else ""
        print(f"  {s.name:<20} {s.value:>10g} {s.unit}{at}")
        print(f"  {'':<20} quote: {s.quote!r}")
        print(f"  {'':<20} from:  {s.source_url}")
    print(f"\norigin: {cand.country_of_origin}\n  quote: {cand.origin_quote!r}")
    print(f"  from:  {cand.origin_source_url}")
    return 0 if cand.status in ("success", "incomplete") else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="real TinyAgent run (costs credit)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-duration", type=int, default=240)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main(args.live, args.max_duration)))
